title: MQTT topics, QoS, and retained messages

questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “MQTT topics, QoS, and retained messages”?
options: A gateway is not mandatory in every deployment; choose architecture for the actual network.
QoS controls delivery guarantees and retransmission behavior.
HTTP is request/response; MQTT is pub/sub.
Devices measure, communication transports data, and services consume it.
questions.answer: QoS controls delivery guarantees and retransmission behavior.
questions.explanation:
QoS controls delivery guarantees and retransmission behavior.
Why: MQTT clients publish and subscribe by topic. QoS 0/1/2 changes delivery behavior; retained messages store the latest value per topic. Topic design affects privacy and scale.

Devices measure, communication transports data, and services consume it.
A gateway is not mandatory in every deployment; choose architecture for the actual network.
questions.answer: Separate command topics from telemetry and restrict who may publish commands.
